findings: The source requires a documented and maintained risk-management system as a continuous iterative lifecycle process for high-risk AI systems.
The legacy action monitor_risk is narrower and less typed than the provision.
The legacy condition includes Unacceptable, although the cited provision is framed for high-risk AI systems.
rules.required_change: Encode establish, implement, document, maintain and iteratively review risk management; replace the coarse High/Unacceptable predicate with current EU high-risk classification logic.

findings: Provider responsibility is supported, but the applicable procedure branches by Annex III category, harmonised standards, common specifications, Annex I product law and substantial modification.
A single High/Unacceptable predicate loses the internal-control versus notified-body routes.
rules.required_change: Add Annex category, applicable standards, product-law and substantial-modification dimensions; encode procedure type and notified-body participation separately.

findings: Provider-side design and identification of human-oversight measures is supported.
The obligation applies to high-risk AI systems and is risk-, autonomy- and context-proportionate; the legacy predicate is too coarse and includes Unacceptable.
rules.required_change: Retain provider design duty but encode high-risk scope, proportionality and the distinct Article 14(3)(a)/(b) implementation pathways.

findings: Deployers must assign human oversight to natural persons with competence, training, authority and support.
The exact duty is more specific than implement_human_oversight and applies to high-risk AI systems.
rules.required_change: Encode assignment, competence, training, authority and support as typed consequences; use current high-risk scope.

findings: Automatic event-recording capability over the system lifetime is supported for high-risk AI systems.
The legacy condition includes Unacceptable and does not retain the traceability purposes or Annex III point 1(a) minimum fields.
rules.required_change: Retain provider-side logging capability while encoding high-risk scope, traceability purpose and category-specific minimum fields.

findings: Deployers must keep automatically generated logs under their control for an appropriate period of at least six months unless other law provides otherwise.
The legacy encoding omits control, minimum retention and legal-exception conditions.
rules.required_change: Add log-control, retention-period and applicable-law exception fields.

findings: Provider disclosure for systems intended to interact directly with natural persons is supported.
The legacy boolean omits the obviousness test, criminal-law exception, timing and accessibility requirements.
rules.required_change: Encode intended direct interaction, obviousness, authorised-law exception, first-interaction timing and accessibility.

findings: The same Article 9 rule and monitor_risk consequence already appear in G1.
Reusing the identical norm as a second obligation group can double-count support and directional divergence.
rules.required_change: Remove the duplicate group or define a distinct temporality projection derived from a typed lifecycle property without counting it as an independent obligation.

findings: The provider self-classification duty before putting the system into use is visually confirmed.
The legacy role and lifecycle predicate is directionally supported but must reference the final risk criteria and catalog.
rules.required_change: Retain the pre-use provider duty and replace the legacy risk-tier schema with the final Law, Decree and Decision 33 classification relation.

findings: The deployer inherits the provider classification result and bears safety and integrity responsibility during use.
When modification, integration or functional change creates new or higher risk, the deployer coordinates with the provider to reclassify.
The legacy encoding assigns the reclassification consequence only to Provider.
rules.required_change: Represent deployer responsibility and provider coordination as separate typed relations rather than a provider-only actor set.

locator.provision: Điều 10 khoản 5 điểm a và khoản 6

findings: High-risk systems are subject to periodic inspection or inspection upon signs of violation.
The paragraph is phrased as an enforcement treatment, while competent-authority action appears in paragraph 6; Regulator as a simple named obligor is an interpretation, not explicit wording.
rules.required_change: Encode inspection trigger and competent-authority enforcement separately; mark actor attribution for independent legal review.

findings: Medium-risk systems are monitored through reporting, sampling inspection or independent assessment.
The legacy action inspect with periodic timing does not represent the provision's alternative mechanisms.
rules.required_change: Encode reporting, sampling and independent-assessment alternatives rather than reusing the high-risk inspection duty.

findings: Conformity assessment before use or after significant change is confirmed for high-risk systems.

Article 13(2)(a) requires certification by a registered or recognised conformity-assessment organisation for catalog systems, while 13(2)(b) permits provider self-assessment or hiring such an organisation for other high-risk systems.
A provider-only consequence flattens third-party assessment and the final Decision 33 route split.
rules.required_change: Encode point-a and point-b routes, assessor role, provider choice and substantial-change retrigger using Decision 33 row identity.

findings: The cited provision requires additional conformity assessment under standards and technical-regulation law when such standards apply.
It does not state that an existing sector certification is automatically reusable as encoded.
rules.required_change: Retract reuse_sector_certification unless a separate final-law provision is identified and encoded with its actual conditions.

findings: The principle states that AI serves humans and does not replace human authority and responsibility, and requires human control and intervention capability over all decisions and behaviour of AI systems.
The source does not expressly name one obligor; UNSPECIFIED_OBLIGOR is appropriate.
The provision is a general statutory principle and should not be silently equated to the complete technical design-and-deployment duties in EU Articles 14 and 26.
rules.required_change: Retain as a general binding human-control principle, but compare it as an analogical/structural duty unless a narrower exact normative-slot crosswalk is independently validated.

findings: Providers of medium- or high-risk systems must notify the classification result through the national AI one-stop portal before use.
This is a classification-notification duty, not a logging or incident-reporting duty comparable to EU Article 12.
rules.required_change: Retain the typed classification-notification duty and remove it from any exact logging/incident obligation pair.

findings: Deployers and users must record the incident, take necessary measures and notify the provider; providers must apply technical measures; providers and deployers coordinate information and response.
The provider or deployer must make the preliminary report, with a specific deployer fallback when the provider cannot be contacted.
The legacy primary/fallback pair omits the distinct record, remediate, coordinate and timed-report duties and overgeneralises the fallback relation.
rules.required_change: Encode separate incident recognition, mitigation, notification, technical remediation, coordination, reporting-deadline and fallback duties.

findings: Providers must design and operate directly interacting AI systems so users recognise that they are interacting with the system, unless otherwise provided by law.
The legacy boolean omits the direct-interaction intent, recognisability outcome and legal exception.
rules.required_change: Encode direct interaction, recognisability and statutory exception explicitly.

locator.provision: No provision stated; nearest relevant source is Điều 19

findings: The policy bundle cites only event-triggered control rather than an article or paragraph.
Article 19 contains multiple serious-incident duties across deployers, users, providers and authorities; it does not create the single generic Deployer control_risk duty encoded here.
The serious-harm trigger also duplicates the G4 incident rule while counting it as a separate obligation group.
rules.required_change: Retract this rule. If temporality remains a research dimension, derive event-triggered timing from the typed Article 19 duties without counting a duplicate independent obligation.

findings: The Guide states a voluntary principle of human accountability and control across AI design, development and deployment.
It is not a universally triggered rule assigning a concrete establish_accountability duty to a named legal actor.
rules.required_change: Model as a voluntary principle object or governance recommendation, not as a rule block equivalent to a statutory obligation.

findings: Human-centricity is a voluntary lifecycle principle and is not expressed as one universally applicable entity-level legal duty.
Treating it as a tautological rule is a modelling choice that must not be confused with statutory applicability.
rules.required_change: Move to the typed ASEAN principle ontology and compare principle coverage separately from binding duties.

findings: The section discusses clear labelling, watermarking, cryptographic provenance and regional policy development as areas for ASEAN to explore.
It does not impose one voluntary label_generated_content rule on every system whose sector equals GenAI.
rules.required_change: Represent content provenance as policy-recommendation dimensions and implementation options; remove the artificial sector predicate.

findings: The Guide describes transparency, disclosure and explainability principles and deployer responsibilities in organisational guidance.
It is not a tautological statutory rule directly equivalent to EU Article 50 or Vietnam Article 11.
rules.required_change: Move to the ASEAN principle/governance layer and use a typed crosswalk rather than direct bindingness comparison.

summary.notice: This audit is a reproducible source-to-encoding review, not independent legal advice or second-reviewer sign-off.
